title: Minerva: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models
paper: Lewkowycz, Andreassen, Dohan, Dyer, Michalewski, Ramasesh, et al. Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models. Google Research, arXiv:2206.14858v2, 2022.
_note: Numbers copied from Tables 1, 3, 4, 5 and Figures 5, 6 of the paper.

content.title: Minerva: language models that solve STEM problems
content.subtitle: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models · Google Research, 2022
content.authors: Lewkowycz et al. · presented by paper2slides demo

slides.notes: The question for this talk: can a language model solve college-level math and science problems without a calculator or any external tool? We follow the recipe, the results, and the memorization check.

content.title: Minerva is PaLM plus 38.5B tokens of technical text
content.caption: Math web pages: 17.5B tokens; arXiv: 21.0B tokens; 5% general text (Table 1).

slides.notes: The novelty is the dataset: natural language next to correct LaTeX. Web pages are cleaned to keep the math notation. The 540B model saw only 26B extra tokens, yet is the best.

content.title: Minerva writes step-by-step LaTeX solutions, not memorized ones
content.meaning: Fig. 1: a MATH question solved by Minerva 62B with a different approach than the ground-truth target
content.caption: Figure 1 from the paper (Lewkowycz et al., 2022)

slides.notes: Read the derivation: point-slope form, simplify, substitute x = 0. The target solution uses y = 4x + b instead. The model output is valid LaTeX with natural language explanations.

content.title: Majority voting saturates quickly, pass@k keeps climbing
content.meaning: Fig. 6: accuracy vs. number of samples k on MATH and GSM8k for pass@k and majority voting
content.caption: Figure 6 from the paper (exact string match, no SymPy)

slides.notes: Majority voting groups samples by final answer and picks the most common. 97% of the large-k accuracy is reached at k = 64 on MATH. Pass@k also counts lucky false positives, so we rely on maj1@k.

content.title: Minerva 540B with majority voting sets new state of the art
content.source: Table 3 (maj1@k: k = 64 on MATH, k = 16 on MMLU-STEM)

slides.notes: MATH jumps from 6.9% published SOTA to 50.3%. GSM8k improves from 74.4% to 78.5% without a calculator. Both continued training and majority voting contribute to the gains.

content.title: Three tests find little evidence of memorization

slides.notes: All three analyses are on MATH with the 62B model. Some MATH problems exist on the web, but they did not pass the data collection process. Voting accuracy stays robust when similar samples are removed.

content.title: Modified problems and filtered samples show no memorization signal
content.meaning: Fig. 5: accuracy on modified vs original questions, and majority-vote accuracy after removing samples similar to the ground truth
content.caption: Figure 5 from the paper (Lewkowycz et al., 2022)

zoom.label: MODIFIED PROBLEMS
zoom.text: Points lie near the diagonal: accuracy ==correlates== with no clear bias for the original wording.

zoom.label: BLEU FILTER
zoom.text: Voting accuracy stays ==flat== once only very dissimilar solutions remain.

slides.notes: Caveat from the appendix: larger framing changes do degrade performance somewhat, but difficulty is hard to control, so the authors do not read this as evidence of memorization.

content.title: Without verification or tools, errors stay hidden
body: No automatic check of the reasoning chain
False positives rise with difficulty: 30% at level 5
Our question: can tools or verifiers fix both?

slides.notes: The last bullet is our own analysis, not from the paper. Table 4 and Table 5 show the errors are mostly reasoning and arithmetic, which a verifier or calculator could target. The paper itself suggests combining with code and formal methods.

content.message: Data, scale and sampling make it work.
takeaways: Little memorization; no verifier or tools

slides.notes: Summarize: the recipe is simple, the gains are large, and the evidence is sober. The remaining gaps are verification and exact calculation.
